cells.tense: You are here, and what you imagined has been felt all the way through.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Take the part of the picture you'd reach for anyway. Work it at a speed that feels good to work at, and stop while it still feels good — no finish line on it.
cells.core:
You can stand outside a whole thing and still be inside it, and what you imagined you have now felt to the end of. The satisfaction isn't counted — it's the plain fact that the shape is complete enough to stand in, which is what the ninth of anything means.
Moving at the pace your feeling can carry is what keeps this steady. Pick the piece you'd reach for anyway, do it at the speed you could hold for a month rather than for a day, and make pace and direction one motion. Then stop while it still feels good, and tomorrow the rhythm carries itself.
cells.sheetLine: The picture is whole, and the pace you keep is your own.
cells.verb: imagining something through to its full felt completion
cells.place: standing outside a whole system while still inside it

cells.tense: You will still be working the finished thing long after it has already ripened.
cells.ask: Look at one finished thing you keep handling. This week, tend nothing there — no upgrades, no check-ins. Then look and see how it stands.
cells.core:
The vision is whole and the satisfaction is real, and some part of you can't stop attending to it. You keep cultivating past the point where anything needs you, and the work has begun to weigh more than the growing did. From where you stand you can see the whole pattern — and from where you stand you also can't stop reworking it.
Care that doesn't exhaust is the way back, and it looks like holding a thing without clutching it. Let one finished piece stay exactly as it ended this week. What grows after that grows because it was tended, not gripped, and your arms will tell you the difference by the weekend.
cells.sheetLine: It's done. Your hands are still on it.

cells.tense: You were one step from a finished thing and you stayed at the edge.
cells.act: write both sides of it on one page and close the page
cells.ask: Set two things you know about the pattern on one page, each its own line, neither one the verdict, then shut the page. Open it later and read both again without picking a winner.
cells.core:
You stand where the whole thing is visible, and you haven't stepped in. The imagining went far and the feeling didn't follow it to the end, so you live at the edge now, at the place where nothing has to be declared. From outside the system you see a great deal. From outside it you commit to nothing.
A quieter knowing charges this. Put the two things you see on one page this week, both true, neither winning yet, and shut the page on both of them. Knowing doesn't have to argue to be real, and the reading you were avoiding turns out to be a page you can close.
cells.sheetLine: You saw the whole thing and stayed at the edge of it.

cells.tense: You are seeing the whole pattern and saying it was nothing you did.
cells.act: sharpen the one skill by repeating its hardest part
cells.ask: Name the pattern-reading you're best at — the call that always turns out right — and find its hardest case. Do that one case deliberately this week, close attention, no shortcuts, and mark that you chose it.
cells.core:
The whole shape is plain to you, and you talk about it as though it were just lying there for anyone. It isn't. Being able to stand outside a system and recognize what's true across its layers is something you do, and it runs under your own name's radar.
The practice that brings this back is quiet and inward. Choose the one discernment you're strongest at and take its hardest case on purpose this week, slow and close, and see the attention it takes from you. Practice that flows without force keeps this connecting instead of isolating. You are the one who sees the pattern. Allow yourself to know that.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing the whole of it and leaving your name off.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has fully imagined and felt a thing into satisfaction; the record's own grammar says such satisfaction is available when this signature appears as a transient, and the seat sees the whole pattern — it does not say the person has received it. A reader could say 'I do see the whole thing, I just don't like it' — and that still passes this cell. The acts of Alignment, Stewardship, Reflection, and Honing are all doable alone in this seat, so each ask stands even if the read is wrong. The sentence that would serve me more than the person is 'You can already see how it all fits' — it flatters the reader and proves nothing, so it is not in the cell.
